title: Pipkin's Moonlit Journey
markdown:
Bramble was a young witch. She sat by her window and hummed a soft tune, practising a new spell. Her little cottage sat high on Cloudneedle Mountain and smelled of lavender and warm spices. She was trying to make the moonlight shine even brighter. She wiggled her fingers. “Moonbeam glow, lend your gentle flow.” The moonbeams outside gathered like wisps of silver dust, swirling, waiting.

A tiny whimper from the sill, so small and sweet, like a sleepy sigh. Bramble’s heart felt a little wobbly.

“Oh, my.” She leaned closer. On the mossy sill sat a little friend, no bigger than her two hands, the softest fluffiest fur, moonlight on snow. Ears long and droopy, velvet petals. Wide gentle eyes, a hint of worry. Another whimper. Lost, far from a cozy home.

Then a caw-caw-caw ruffled the quiet. Gareth the crow, feathers dark and shiny, landed on the roof and peered down with clever eyes.

“Lost, is it?” A dry rustle. “Just a little lost thing. Best to leave it be. More time for crow-things.”

Bramble shook her head. Soft braids swayed. “No, Gareth. It looks a little sad and worried. It needs to find its home, not be left alone.” She opened the window. Old wood creaked. The fluffy friend hopped in, little feet tapping, nudged her hand. Fur like a warm gentle cloud. She decided to call it Pipkin. It looked like a little berry, round and sweet. A gentle kindness bloomed. Pipkin needed to be home, safe, before the stars all settled down for rest.

“Alright, Pipkin. We’ll help you find your way. Gareth, can you try to be helpful for once? We need your know-how.”

Gareth ruffled. “Helpful? I am always helpful! I know all the paths in the Cloudneedle Mountains. Follow me, and I’ll have you there soon!” Another caw, and he swooped into the dimming twilight.

Bramble scooped Pipkin up. Soft warm weight. Tiny heart beating a small brave drum. Sensible boots on the path, which knew the mountain better than Gareth’s leaf did. Tall pines seemed to sigh secrets, then think better of telling them all at once. Pine needles, cool clean mist. The scent always made her feel calm. Pipkin watched the dark between the trunks as if it might contain supper, or home, or both.

After a little while Gareth stopped on a low branch, puzzled. “Hmm. This doesn’t look quite right. My map seems a little muddled.” He held up a crumpled brown leaf that looked mostly like a very happy bird’s lunch. Bramble peered. Indeed muddled.

A soft voice, tiny silver bells. “Perhaps I can help?” Elara, a kind elf, eyes like dewdrops, cloak woven with leaves and tiny wildflowers. “You look like you are on a journey, little witch.” Smile as warm as sunshine on a cloudy day.

Bramble explained about Pipkin. Gareth chimed, “She’s trying to find its home, but my map is all wrong. We need the right path!”

Elara unfurled a real map, fine soft paper, winding trails, little drawings of sleepy flowers that looked as if they might snore if you listened. “Pipkin lives near the Whispering Falls. A little further, past the sleeping stones.” She tapped the paper. The stones on the map were drawn with closed eyes, which Bramble found polite.

“Thank you, Elara!” Bramble’s heart lighter. “Come on, Pipkin, we’re almost there.” She tried to coax a walk. Pipkin sat down politely on the forest floor, blinked, and with a tiny shake of the head politely refused to budge.

“Oh, no, no, no.” Gareth flapped. “Stubborn! They always are, these fluffy ones. Give him a little push!”

Bramble smiled a small understanding smile. She knew Pipkin wasn’t being stubborn. He was just a little tired from his journey and perhaps a little unsure of the new path, which had more stones than a windowsill does. “It’s alright, Pipkin. A long walk for little legs, and you’re a little tired, aren’t you? Maybe you can ride with me for a little while longer.” She lifted him again. Snuggle, a comforting weight. The politely stubborn passenger who would not walk and would not complain made her giggle, a quiet happy sound that echoed softly through the trees. Gareth muttered that giggling was not a map skill. Elara pretended not to hear, which is also a map skill.

Elara’s lantern cast a warm friendly light through a grove where the air filled with the gentle musical murmur of running water. Nestled in emerald moss: little homes that looked just like Pipkin, if Pipkin had been a doorway. A larger Pipkin, same moonlight fur, long droopy ears, peeked from a cozy doorway. “Pipkin! Oh, my little wanderer!” Relief and joy. Pipkin wriggled, hopped down, squeaks and nuzzles, a supper-smell of crushed berries on the step. Bramble watched, warm as a steaming mug of cocoa on a chilly evening, and did not hurry the nuzzles.

“Thank you, Bramble, and thank you, dear Elara. We were so worried when he didn’t come home for his supper.”

Gareth, preening on a nearby branch with great self-importance, huffed. “Well, I knew where it was all along, really. Just testing your observation skills.”

Elara smiled at him, then at Bramble, and did not make a speech about kind hearts. She waved them onto a clear easy path toward the cottage. The way back felt quicker. Night sounds. A crow who had been useful in spite of his map.

In her room Bramble tucked Pipkin onto a velvety cushion near the hearth. Wait. Pipkin had gone home. She tucked the empty thought away and set a small extra cushion there anyway, in case of windowsills. Sleepy embers. She looked out at the velvet sky, a million stars, moonlight silver across toys and books that looked as if they were sleeping too. Blankets. Heavy lids. Dreams of soft fur and whispering pines, and of a crow who would claim, tomorrow, that the leaf had been a perfectly good map all along.
characters: Bramble (young witch), Gareth (crow), Pipkin (fluffy friend), Elara (elf)
author: StoryGen Community
